I am 60 years old and have farmed this land for 36 years. My back is not what it used to be, and with only two of us in the household, I must be careful with my labor. I know this soil of Quzhou County like the back of my hand.

This year, I will put 12 mu into my wheat-maize rotation because that is our bread and butter. I will buy improved wheat seed from the shop in town — the new varieties resist lodging and give steady yields. I will rotary till before planting wheat in October. For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress with urea in spring when the wheat wakes up. I have my well, so I will irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat can survive the cold, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once at grain filling. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. After harvest in early June, I must move fast. I will plant hybrid maize seed right away with no-tillage to save time and diesel — the season is short and I cannot afford to let the land sit. Maize needs two good irrigations in summer, at the big trumpet leaf stage and at filling. I will spray twice for pests on both crops, that is usually enough.

For cotton, I keep only 3 mu because picking it by hand at my age is hard, hard work, and my husband's knees are no better than mine. I will plough that field deep in spring and plant the cotton seeds I saved from last year — they have done well for me and I do not need to spend cash on new seed. Cotton does not need as much fertilizer as the grain crops, but it needs more pesticide. The bollworms and aphids always come, so I will spray three times. I will irrigate twice when the dry spells hit in July and August. I hope for about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

This is my plan. I have done it many times. I trust my experience more than books.
